correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the quotient without relying on a set-theoretic identification of determinantal schemes. On the chart p_ab=1 take pivot columns e_1,e_2 and remaining columns (x_i,y_i). Signs act as (s_a s_i x_i,s_b s_i y_i), equivalently independent simultaneous flips of each pair plus one common flip of all y coordinates. Invariants under the pair flips are generated by x_i²,y_i²,x_i y_i. The remaining invariants add (x_i y_i)(x_j y_j), which is one-half of x_i²y_j²+x_j²y_i²−(x_i y_j−x_j y_i)². Hence the projective square-image chart is exactly the invariant quotient chart, including at points with zero coordinates. Finite invariants give normality and the characteristic-zero finite quotient theorem gives Cohen–Macaulayness. Every stabilizing sign splits the fixed two-plane into two lines or has it entirely in one sign eigenspace. The images are the mixed Segre and coordinate zero-row loci, respectively, and the negative tangent dimensions from Hom(W,C^n/W) are n−2 for mixed and twice the opposite sign-block size otherwise. No stabilizer has a pseudoreflection, so the formal finite quotient is smooth exactly for trivial stabilizer. The generic mixed support has all cross edges and determines its unordered bipartition; a generic zero-row point has every other edge and cannot be mixed since the other indices contain a triangle. These generic points distinguish the components and have just the displayed order-two stabilizer. The transverse negative coordinates in a mixed chart can be taken as minor-to-major column-coordinate ratios with pivots on opposite sides; they all transform by the common relative sign, independently of the sign action on the major coordinates. At the generic zero-row locus take both pivots away from the missing column. Divide its y coordinate by a nonzero y_i/x_i from a remaining column to make both missing-column coordinates transform by the same sign, independent of the base action. Thus the transverse quotient types also split over the generic residue fields. All ages are at least one; the zero-row generic age equals one, so canonical but not terminal. Small-group Gorensteinness is the determinant-one criterion: only the mixed negative dimension can be odd, exactly when n is odd. The dimensions, n+2^(n−1)−1 count, and n=5 example follow.
residual_risks: The finite-field spot checks do not establish the complex quotient or classify all strata. This proof concerns generic transverse quotients and reduced support, not scheme-theoretic Jacobian components or deeper crossing germs.

evidence: The determinantal model together with the known rank-two Segre decomposition makes the E portion of the support closely tied to prior work: lower-rank points annihilate the first derivatives of every defining 4×4 minor. The n=4 record uses the same quotient approach and proves A1 models in that special dimension. The rank-two chart theorem computes the intrinsic local rings of that reducible rank-two scheme, not the transverse local rings inside X_n.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Credit the Segre list and its rank-drop singularity as covered or immediate. The complete support also needs the smoothness/singularity distinction within rank three; the two transverse quotient types and local canonical and Gorenstein criteria require controlling the representation of each stabilizing sign in arbitrary n. The n=4 case has transverse dimension two in both families and cannot imply the distinction or the odd-n failure of Gorensteinness.

value.rationale: The squared Grassmannian is a natural structured rank locus with established equations. The intrinsic singularity classification determines which coordinate omissions and bipartitions fail smoothness, how their generic transverse dimensions differ, and whether the canonical sheaf is locally free. The dimension dependence and Gorenstein parity are not visible at n=4 and distinguish geometric features the equations and smaller rank-locus list did not quantify.
residual_risks: No classification of deeper intersections, higher Grassmannian ranks, or characteristic two is asserted.
